newsitem.title: UK: Thorn drops after credit deals criticism. [CORRECTED 9:53 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Thorn drops after credit deals criticism. [CORRECTED 9:53 GMT]

text.p: Shares in retail group Thorn Plc fell in early trading on Monday after the stock went ex-dividend and a report in the Mail on Sunday newspaper said the company was under scrutiny from local trading standards officers for its credit deals. (Corrects to show shares went ex-dividend this morning)
The stock was quoted down 9-1/2p at 167-1/2 by 0828 GMT in thin volume of 3,358 shares. (Updates share price and volume)

The paper said Thorn's Crazy George's chain, which targets low earners and those on benefits, had been criticised for its "option service cover" offer which raised the interest rate on transactions to more than 80 percent from an advertised 29.9 percent.
No-one at Thorn was immediately available for comment.
A spokesman for the Office of Fair Trading confirmed that trading standards officers had raised concerns relating to Crazy George's but declined further comment on grounds of confidentiality.
